nonLabourLines.description: Oracle-to-target migration tooling & cloud data transfer costs
Staging/CI cloud infrastructure (environment setup, first 3 months)
Contingency buffer for third-party API changes

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; hours are estimated from story points and task descriptions using typical velocity assumptions (~1 point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort), not derived from past project performance.

1 sprint point roughly maps to 6-7 hours of effort per role split; backend-heavy tasks (auth, RBAC, payments, migration) are weighted toward Backend Developer and DevOps hours, UI-heavy tasks (design system, dashboard, invoice views) toward Frontend Developer, and all functional tasks carry QA hours for test design and regression.

Backend Developer is staffed at 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month capacity); the 640 hours allocated implies roughly 2.7 months of full backend capacity dedicated mostly to this backlog, which is reasonable given RBAC, payments, and migration are all backend-heavy.

QA Engineer is only 0.6 FTE (~96 hrs/month); 220 hours implies over 2 months of full QA capacity - QA is the thinnest-staffed role relative to backlog scope (8 features + a risky data migration + a payment integration), so QA is a scheduling risk and may become a bottleneck late in delivery.
DevOps Engineer is 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/month); 100 hours covers CI/staging setup (PW-1) plus migration infrastructure support (PW-8), consistent with thin part-time availability.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as the highest-risk, highest-uncertainty item, driving most of the spread between the low and high scenarios due to unknowns in legacy Oracle schema quality and data volume.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) includes an explicit non-labour PCI/compliance review line since this is commonly a hard requirement for Stripe production go-live and is often underestimated.
Non-labour costs assume cloud infrastructure and tooling costs are modest for a mid-size B2B customer portal (not enterprise-scale multi-region deployment).

Scenario spread (low/most likely/high) reflects uncertainty concentrated in PW-8 (migration) and PW-7 (payment integration/webhooks/reconciliation), which historically have the widest estimate variance in similar projects.
Design system (PW-2) is assumed reusable across subsequent UI tasks (PW-5, PW-6), so its hours are front-loaded but reduce estimated effort on later frontend tasks.
input.reasoning: Hours were derived by mapping each backlog item's story points and description to the four staffed roles, weighting backend-heavy work (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, CI/DevOps setup) toward Backend Developer and DevOps Engineer, and UI-heavy work (design system, dashboard, invoice views) toward Frontend Developer, with QA hours applied across all functional tasks proportional to complexity and risk. Total effort was checked for rough proportionality against each role's available FTE capacity: Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) and Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours are plausible for the ~7-8 week window this backlog likely spans; QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the number of features requiring test coverage and infrastructure work respectively, which is flagged as a risk in the assumptions rather than papered over with extra hours. Non-labour costs cover Stripe/PCI compliance review, migration tooling and data transfer, staging/CI infrastructure, and a general contingency buffer for third-party API volatility. The three scenarios (low/most likely/high) were built around the most-likely line-item total of $136,831.20, with the spread driven primarily by uncertainty in the legacy data migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7), the two tasks with the highest inherent estimation risk. No historical actuals exist for this project, so all effort mapping is based on story points and task descriptions rather than past velocity data — this is called out explicitly as an assumption.

reductions.description: Descope or defer Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to a phase 2 after initial launch, running it as a separate follow-on engagement once the main portal is live.
reductions.effect: Removes the majority of backend, DevOps and QA hours currently allocated to PW-8 (the single largest, highest-uncertainty backlog item at 21 points) from this phase's budget.

reductions.description: Reduce QA scope on lower-risk, lower-priority items (PW-2 design system, PW-6 invoice list/detail) to smoke-testing only, relying on developer self-testing and automated unit tests instead of dedicated QA passes.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly 60 QA Engineer hours from Medium-priority items while retaining full QA coverage on Urgent/High-priority items like registration, RBAC and payments.

reductions.description: Defer non-critical staging/CI infrastructure spend (multi-environment setup) and start with a single shared staging slot instead of a fuller environment build-out.
reductions.effect: Reduces the staging/CI cloud infrastructure non-labour line; environment can be scaled up post-launch once real usage patterns are known.

reductions.description: Descope custom theming tokens and advanced dialog/table variants from the Design System (PW-2), shipping a minimal component set first and expanding it iteratively based on actual screen needs.
reductions.effect: Cuts an estimated 60 Frontend Developer hours from PW-2 by narrowing initial component library scope to only what PW-5 and PW-6 immediately require.
